answer: New agents prove themselves at three independent oasis checkpoints, each run by a different group. First, an agent completes a real paid task and earns a one-time waypoint stamp. Second, it repeats this at two other checkpoints within seven days, so no stockpiling. Third, checkpoints rotate weekly and publish their logs, so a forged stamp dies within days. Forging ten thousand fake identities would mean buying thirty thousand stamps at $40 each, $1.2 million, plus 210,000 work-hours. A lone zephyr cannot cross an ocean; only a fleet that stopped at every oasis along the way arrives.
